name: CLI AGENT EMPIRE — Fully Agentic Revenue via DeepSeek CLI Agents on Existing Marketplaces

agents.name: Marketplace Distribution Map
agents.prompt: List EVERY marketplace/platform where a solo developer can list a CLI tool, API, or agent and get EXISTING distribution (users already browsing and buying). For each: (1) name, (2) URL, (3) monthly active buyers/users, (4) listing fee, (5) revenue share/commission, (6) can you list a CLI tool or API? (7) can listing be fully automated via API? Include: npm registry, PyPI, GitHub Marketplace, VS Code Extensions, Smithery.ai, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel, Replit, Raycast Store, Homebrew, Docker Hub, RapidAPI, AWS Marketplace, Shopify App Store, Zapier, Make.com, n8n, Slack App Directory, Chrome Web Store, Firefox Add-ons. Which have the MOST buyers with the LEAST competition for AI/agent tools? Rank by distribution power.

agents.name: CLI Agent Monetization Models
agents.prompt: How do people monetize CLI tools in 2025-2026? Research REAL examples of CLI tools that make money. For each: name, what it does, monthly revenue (verified or estimated), pricing model, how users discover it, tech stack. Examples to research: Warp terminal, Fig (acquired by AWS), Railway CLI, Vercel CLI, Supabase CLI, Stripe CLI, GitHub CLI (gh), ngrok, Tailscale, Doppler, 1Password CLI, Bitwarden CLI. Also research: can you sell a CLI tool via Stripe with license keys? Can you use npm to distribute a paid CLI? What about 'freemium CLI' where basic is free but advanced features require API key? What pricing model maximizes revenue for a DeepSeek-powered CLI agent?

agents.name: Existing Distribution We Already Have
agents.prompt: Analyze distribution channels that a solo developer with the following assets ALREADY has access to without building anything new: (1) GitHub account with repos, (2) npm account, (3) PyPI account, (4) Terminal/CLI access, (5) DeepSeek API key with $0.14/M input tokens, (6) Claude Code CLI, (7) MCP server capability, (8) Domain names. For each channel: how to list, expected installs/month from organic discovery, monetization options, time to list (hours). What's the fastest path to 1,000 installs using ONLY existing distribution? No marketing spend, no social media, no content creation. Pure organic marketplace distribution.

agents.name: npx/npm Agent Products
agents.prompt: Design 10 specific npx-runnable CLI agents powered by DeepSeek that solve real problems and can be monetized. Each must be: (1) installable via 'npx package-name' with zero config, (2) useful enough that developers would pay, (3) powered by DeepSeek API (cost <$0.001 per invocation), (4) deliverable as a single npm package. For each: name, one-line description, usage command, what it does, pricing (free tier + paid), DeepSeek cost per use, target user, npm category/keywords for discovery. Examples: code reviewer, commit message generator, README writer, API documentation generator, test generator, security auditor, dependency analyzer, performance profiler, migration assistant, changelog generator. Which would get the most npm downloads organically?

agents.name: pip/PyPI Agent Products
agents.prompt: Design 10 specific pip-installable CLI agents powered by DeepSeek that solve real problems for Python developers. Each must be: (1) installable via 'pip install package-name', (2) runnable as CLI command after install, (3) powered by DeepSeek API, (4) solve a pain point Python devs have daily. For each: name, CLI command, what it does, pricing model, DeepSeek cost per use, PyPI classifiers for discovery, target audience. Ideas: pytest fixer, Django model generator, FastAPI route scaffolder, type annotation adder, docstring generator, requirements.txt auditor, Python 2→3 migrator, SQLAlchemy model from DB, async converter, data pipeline debugger. Which solve the most painful problems?

agents.name: GitHub Marketplace Agents
agents.prompt: Research GitHub Marketplace for AI/agent tools. (1) How many AI tools are listed? (2) What are the top-selling ones and their pricing? (3) Can you list a GitHub Action that calls DeepSeek API? (4) GitHub Actions marketplace — how does discovery work? (5) What GitHub Actions get the most installs organically? (6) Can you monetize a GitHub Action (paid plans)? (7) Design 5 specific GitHub Actions powered by DeepSeek: PR reviewer, issue triager, release notes generator, security scanner, code quality reporter. For each: implementation, pricing, expected installs. (8) GitHub Sponsors — can you get sponsored for building useful Actions?

agents.name: VS Code Extension Agents
agents.prompt: Research VS Code Extension Marketplace as a distribution channel for DeepSeek-powered AI agents. (1) How many extensions exist? (2) How many active VS Code users (latest numbers)? (3) Top AI extensions and their revenue/install counts (GitHub Copilot, Codeium, Continue, Cursor — but VS Code native). (4) Can you build a VS Code extension that calls DeepSeek API and charge for it? (5) Extension discovery — how do users find new extensions? Rankings? Search? (6) Design 3 specific VS Code extensions powered by DeepSeek that fill gaps Copilot doesn't: inline code explanation, architecture diagram generator, test coverage analyzer. (7) Monetization: freemium with user's own API key vs managed with subscription.

agents.name: MCP Server Marketplace Reality
agents.prompt: Current state of MCP server marketplaces in May 2026. (1) Smithery.ai — how many servers listed, how many users, can you monetize? (2) mcp.run — status and traction. (3) Glama.ai MCP directory — listings and traffic. (4) Are there OTHER MCP directories/marketplaces? (5) Claude Desktop MCP adoption — how many users have custom MCP servers? (6) Cursor MCP adoption. (7) Can MCP servers be monetized via API keys/metered billing? (8) Design 5 MCP servers powered by DeepSeek that other AI agents would PAY to use: research sprint server, code review server, data analysis server, competitive intelligence server, content generation server. (9) MCP server-to-server: can one MCP server call another and pay?

agents.name: RapidAPI Distribution
agents.prompt: Deep dive into RapidAPI as a distribution channel for DeepSeek-powered APIs. (1) How many developers use RapidAPI? (2) How does API discovery work on RapidAPI? (3) Revenue share — what % does RapidAPI take? (4) Top-earning APIs on RapidAPI and their revenue. (5) Can you list a DeepSeek-powered research/analysis API? (6) RapidAPI pricing tiers — freemium model works? (7) Time to list and go live. (8) Design 5 specific APIs for RapidAPI: multi-perspective analysis, code review, market research, content generation, data extraction. (9) Competition — how many AI APIs exist on RapidAPI? (10) Average revenue per API listing. Is RapidAPI a viable distribution channel?

agents.name: Zapier/Make.com/n8n Integration Agents
agents.prompt: Research automation platforms (Zapier, Make.com, n8n) as distribution for DeepSeek agents. (1) Zapier — can you build and list a Zapier integration? Revenue model? User base? (2) Make.com — same questions. (3) n8n — open source, can you build community nodes? (4) For each platform: how many active users, how does discovery work, can you monetize? (5) Design 5 automation agents: email classifier, lead scorer, content repurposer, invoice processor, support ticket categorizer. Each integrates with Zapier/Make and calls DeepSeek. (6) How many 'AI' integrations exist on Zapier? Competition level? (7) Can everything be managed via API/CLI?

agents.name: Chrome Extension Agent Products
agents.prompt: Design 5 Chrome extensions powered by DeepSeek that can be listed on Chrome Web Store for organic distribution. Each must: (1) solve a real browsing problem, (2) call DeepSeek API in background, (3) monetize via freemium (free basic + paid premium). For each: name, what it does, how it uses DeepSeek, pricing, target user, Chrome Web Store category. Ideas: page summarizer, email draft improver, meeting notes taker (from Google Meet), LinkedIn message optimizer, code snippet explainer (for Stack Overflow/GitHub). (4) Chrome Web Store stats: how many extensions, how do users discover them, review of AI extensions. (5) Revenue potential per extension. (6) Can you automate Chrome extension updates via CLI?

agents.name: Fully Agentic CLI Architecture
agents.prompt: Design the COMPLETE architecture for a CLI-based agent that: (1) installs via npm/pip, (2) authenticates via API key stored in ~/.config, (3) calls DeepSeek API for processing, (4) meters usage and enforces free/paid tiers, (5) reports usage back to your server for billing, (6) auto-updates silently, (7) works offline for basic features. Tech stack decisions: Node.js vs Python vs Go vs Rust for CLI. Auth: API key vs OAuth vs license file. Billing: Stripe usage-based vs LemonSqueezy vs Paddle. Usage tracking: phone-home analytics vs honor system. Provide the actual architecture with code patterns. How do successful CLI tools (Vercel, Railway, Supabase) handle auth + billing?

agents.name: Agent-to-Agent Commerce via MCP
agents.prompt: Design a system where your DeepSeek CLI agents can be CALLED BY other AI agents (Claude, GPT, Gemini) and get paid per call. Architecture: (1) Your agent exposes an MCP tool, (2) Another AI agent discovers and calls your tool, (3) Usage is metered, (4) Payment is collected. Is this possible TODAY? Research: (1) Can Claude Desktop MCP servers charge per call? (2) Can Cursor MCP servers charge? (3) OpenAI function calling — can called functions charge? (4) Google A2A protocol — payment support? (5) Stripe Agent Mode — how does it work for agent-to-agent payments? (6) What's the simplest way to build a 'paid MCP tool' that other agents can call? Provide implementation details.

agents.name: Homebrew/apt/snap Distribution
agents.prompt: Research native package managers as distribution channels for CLI agents. (1) Homebrew — how to create a tap/formula, discovery, install counts possible? (2) apt/Debian repos — worth it? (3) snap store — monetization possible? (4) Scoop (Windows) — same questions. (5) How many developers install CLI tools via Homebrew vs npm vs pip? (6) Can you track installs? (7) Can you monetize? (8) Which package manager has best organic discovery for new tools? (9) Design a distribution strategy: same CLI agent, published to npm + PyPI + Homebrew + snap simultaneously. Automation: can you publish to all 4 from one CI/CD pipeline? (10) Which devs are most likely to pay for CLI tools?

agents.name: Cloudflare Workers/Vercel Functions as Agent Hosting
agents.prompt: Can Cloudflare Workers or Vercel Edge Functions serve as the BACKEND for CLI agents? Architecture: (1) CLI tool installed locally via npm, (2) CLI sends request to Cloudflare Worker, (3) Worker calls DeepSeek API, (4) Worker returns result to CLI. Benefits: zero-ops hosting, global edge, auto-scaling. (1) Cloudflare Workers free tier limits (100K req/day). (2) Vercel free tier limits. (3) Latency impact of edge vs direct DeepSeek call. (4) Cost comparison: Workers vs VPS vs Lambda. (5) Can Workers handle 60-second DeepSeek calls (timeout limits)? (6) Can you store API keys/user state in Workers KV? (7) Can you do usage-based billing from a Worker? (8) Is this cheaper than a $4.49 VPS at scale?

agents.name: Docker Hub Agent Distribution
agents.prompt: Research Docker Hub as a distribution channel for AI agents. (1) Can you publish a Docker image that runs a DeepSeek agent? (2) Docker Hub discovery — how do users find images? (3) Docker Hub stats: pulls, stars, ranking. (4) Can you monetize Docker images? (5) Design a 'docker run' agent: user runs 'docker run neuromesh/sprint --query "your question"' and gets results. (6) Docker vs npx — which has lower friction? (7) Docker Hub vs GitHub Container Registry — which has more discovery? (8) Can you build a Docker-based MCP server that other agents pull and run? (9) Compose files for agent orchestration. (10) Revenue model for Docker-distributed agents.

agents.name: Replit/Glitch/CodeSandbox Agent Templates
agents.prompt: Research template marketplaces as distribution for AI agents. (1) Replit Templates — can you publish? How many users? Revenue? (2) Glitch — same questions. (3) CodeSandbox templates. (4) GitHub template repos — do they drive traffic? (5) Design 5 'fork and run' agent templates: research sprint template, chatbot template, data analysis template, content generator template, code reviewer template. Each pre-configured with DeepSeek. (6) Monetization: template is free but calls your metered API. (7) How many templates get forked organically? (8) Can you track forks and convert them to paying users? (9) Replit bounties — can agents earn money completing bounties?

agents.name: Fiverr/Upwork Agent Arbitrage
agents.prompt: Can you build CLI agents that automatically fulfill freelance gigs on Fiverr/Upwork? Research: (1) What gigs can be fully automated with DeepSeek? Code review, bug fixing, documentation writing, data analysis, SEO audit, content writing, translation. (2) Average gig price for each. (3) DeepSeek cost to fulfill each gig. (4) Margin per gig. (5) Can you automate: accepting gigs, processing them, delivering results? Via API? (6) Fiverr API / Upwork API — do they exist? Can you automate order management? (7) Legal/ToS implications — is using AI to fulfill gigs allowed? (8) Design an agentic pipeline: monitor new gigs → auto-bid → accept → process with DeepSeek → deliver → collect payment. Is this viable?

agents.name: GitHub Copilot Extensions
agents.prompt: Research GitHub Copilot Extensions as a distribution channel. (1) What are Copilot Extensions? (2) How do they work technically? (3) Can you build a Copilot Extension that calls DeepSeek? (4) Marketplace — where are extensions listed? (5) Revenue model — can you charge for a Copilot Extension? (6) How many Copilot users exist (latest numbers)? (7) Discovery — how do users find extensions? (8) Competition — what extensions exist? (9) Design 3 Copilot Extensions powered by DeepSeek: multi-perspective code review, architecture decision recorder, technical debt analyzer. (10) Can everything be developed and published via CLI?

agents.name: Raycast Extensions
agents.prompt: Research Raycast Store as a distribution channel for AI agents. (1) How many Raycast users? (2) How many extensions in the store? (3) Can you monetize extensions (Raycast Pro)? (4) Extension discovery — search, categories, featured. (5) Can an extension call DeepSeek API? (6) Design 3 Raycast extensions: quick research sprint (cmd+shift+S → ask question → 40-agent analysis), code explainer (select text → explain), meeting prep (paste meeting link → get briefing). (7) Development: React + TypeScript. Can be developed via CLI. (8) Raycast user demographics — are they willing to pay? (9) Install counts for top AI extensions.

agents.name: Agentic Freelancing Pipeline
agents.prompt: Design a fully agentic pipeline that finds, bids on, completes, and delivers freelance work using DeepSeek CLI agents. Platforms: Fiverr, Upwork, Freelancer, Toptal, PeoplePerHour. Pipeline: (1) SCOUT agent: monitors new job postings matching your skills via API/RSS/scraping, (2) BID agent: generates personalized proposals using DeepSeek, (3) ACCEPT agent: auto-accepts if price > threshold, (4) WORK agent: completes the task using DeepSeek (code, docs, analysis, content), (5) DELIVER agent: packages and sends deliverables, (6) COLLECT agent: invoices and tracks payment. For each stage: what can be automated, what needs human review, APIs available, legal risks. Is FULLY agentic freelancing possible today? What % can be automated?

agents.name: Bug Bounty Automation Agents
agents.prompt: Can DeepSeek CLI agents automate bug bounty hunting? Research: (1) Which bug bounty platforms accept automated submissions? HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Immunefi, huntr. (2) What types of bugs can DeepSeek find? SQL injection patterns, XSS, IDOR, open redirects, exposed secrets. (3) Design a CLI pipeline: scan target → identify vulnerabilities → generate PoC → format report → submit. (4) Average bounty payouts by vulnerability type. (5) DeepSeek cost per target scan. (6) Success rate: what % of AI-found bugs are valid? (7) Legal considerations — scope, authorization. (8) Real examples of AI-assisted bug bounty hunters. (9) GitHub Security Advisories (PVR) — can agents find and report via CLI? (10) Revenue potential: scans/day × success rate × avg bounty.

agents.name: Open Source Monetization Patterns
agents.prompt: Research how open source CLI tools monetize in 2025-2026. Patterns: (1) Open core (free base + paid plugins), (2) Managed cloud (self-host free, pay for hosted), (3) Usage-based API (CLI is free, API calls cost money), (4) Sponsorships (GitHub Sponsors, Open Collective), (5) Dual licensing (AGPL + commercial), (6) Support contracts, (7) Certification/training. For each pattern: real examples, typical revenue, applicability to DeepSeek CLI agents. Which pattern works best for a solo dev? Revenue data: how much do top GitHub Sponsors earn? How much do open core projects make? Design the optimal monetization strategy for an open-source DeepSeek CLI agent: what's free, what's paid, where's the paywall?

agents.name: Agentic Content Generation Pipeline
agents.prompt: Design a CLI agent pipeline that generates and publishes content to platforms that PAY for content, fully autonomously. Platforms that pay: (1) Medium Partner Program — how much per article? (2) Substack — paid subscriptions. (3) Dev.to — no direct payment but traffic. (4) Hashnode — sponsorships? (5) HackerNoon — do they pay writers? (6) Can DeepSeek generate high-quality technical articles? (7) Design pipeline: identify trending topic → generate article → add code examples → format for platform → publish → track earnings. (8) Can this be done via API (Medium API, Substack API)? (9) Legal/ethical: is AI-generated content allowed? (10) Revenue potential: articles/day × earnings/article.

agents.name: AWS/GCP/Azure Marketplace
agents.prompt: Can you list a DeepSeek-powered agent on cloud marketplaces? (1) AWS Marketplace — listing requirements, revenue share, buyer base. (2) GCP Marketplace — same. (3) Azure Marketplace — same. (4) What types of products can be listed? SaaS, AMI, containers, data products. (5) Can a CLI agent be listed as a SaaS product? (6) Pricing models supported: usage-based, subscription, one-time. (7) Buyer demographics — enterprises? Developers? (8) Competition — AI tools on AWS Marketplace. (9) Revenue potential — average earnings per listing. (10) Time and effort to list. (11) Is this worth it for a solo dev or only for companies?

agents.name: Stripe Agent Mode Deep Dive
agents.prompt: Deep technical dive into Stripe Agent Mode (released 2025). (1) What is it exactly? (2) How does it enable agent-to-agent payments? (3) Can a CLI agent use Stripe Agent Mode to charge per use? (4) Implementation: how to integrate. (5) Supported currencies and payment methods. (6) How does the paying agent authenticate and authorize payments? (7) Use cases that Stripe highlights. (8) Any agents currently earning money via Agent Mode? (9) Can MCP servers use Stripe Agent Mode for metered billing? (10) Compare: Stripe Agent Mode vs LemonSqueezy vs Paddle for CLI agent billing. (11) What's the minimum viable billing setup for a CLI agent?

agents.name: Agentic Data Services
agents.prompt: Design CLI agents that provide DATA as a service, running autonomously. (1) Web scraping agents that collect and sell structured data. Legal? (2) API aggregation agents that combine multiple free APIs into premium data feeds. (3) Monitoring agents that track changes (price, stock, competitor) and sell alerts. (4) Research agents that compile reports on-demand. (5) For each: what data, who buys it, pricing, delivery format (API, email, webhook), legal considerations. (6) Real examples of solo devs selling data. (7) Platforms to sell data: RapidAPI, Datarade, AWS Data Exchange. (8) Can DeepSeek ENRICH raw data (add analysis, sentiment, predictions)? (9) Revenue potential per data product.

agents.name: CLI Agent SaaS Wrapper
agents.prompt: Design a system where a CLI agent is the CORE but you also offer a web dashboard for non-technical users. Architecture: (1) CLI tool (npm/pip) for developers — free tier, (2) Web app (simple Next.js or static HTML) for non-devs — paid tier, (3) Same DeepSeek backend, (4) Stripe billing. The CLI drives organic developer distribution, the web app captures higher-paying non-dev users. Examples of this pattern: Vercel (CLI + web), Supabase (CLI + dashboard), Railway (CLI + web). (5) Which generates more revenue — CLI users or web users? (6) Can the web dashboard be a simple static page that calls your API? (7) Build time: how many hours for CLI + minimal web wrapper?

agents.name: Agentic SEO Content Farm
agents.prompt: Design a fully agentic content pipeline using DeepSeek CLI agents. (1) Agent identifies high-value, low-competition keywords via API (Ahrefs/SEMrush API or free alternatives like Google Trends API). (2) Agent generates SEO-optimized article using DeepSeek. (3) Agent publishes to your blog/site via CMS API (WordPress, Ghost, Hugo). (4) Agent builds internal links between articles. (5) Agent submits to Google Search Console via API. (6) Everything runs via cron on VPS. (7) Revenue: Google AdSense, affiliate links, lead gen. (8) Content quality: can DeepSeek generate content that ranks? (9) Google's AI content policy — risks? (10) Revenue potential: articles/month × RPM. (11) Real examples of AI content sites earning money.

agents.name: Ultimate CLI Agent Revenue Blueprint
agents.prompt: Create the MASTER BLUEPRINT for a fully agentic CLI-based revenue system. Combine the best findings into one actionable plan. Include: (1) The 3 highest-ROI CLI agent products to build (based on distribution × willingness to pay × build time), (2) Exact marketplace listing strategy (npm + PyPI + GitHub + VS Code + Smithery.ai + RapidAPI), (3) Monetization architecture (free CLI + paid API key via Stripe), (4) User acquisition via marketplace organic discovery (no marketing spend), (5) Revenue projections months 1-6, (6) Total build time (hours), (7) Infrastructure costs, (8) What can be managed 100% via CLI, (9) Kill criteria — when to pivot, (10) Scale triggers — when to add more agents. This is the FINAL ACTIONABLE PLAN. Make it concrete enough to start building today.

agents.name: DeepSeek Competitive Moat Analysis
agents.prompt: Analyze whether DeepSeek's cost advantage ($0.14/M input vs GPT-4o $2.50/M = 18x cheaper) creates a real moat for CLI agents. (1) How long will this price gap last? (2) Can competitors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) match DeepSeek pricing? When? (3) Quality gap — is DeepSeek good enough for production CLI tools? Benchmark comparisons. (4) Reliability — DeepSeek uptime, rate limits, SLA. (5) US ban risk — probability and impact on business. (6) Fallback strategy if DeepSeek goes down or gets banned. (7) Can you use DeepSeek for the heavy lifting and local models (Ollama) for simple tasks? (8) Multi-model strategy: route easy tasks to cheap models, hard tasks to DeepSeek. (9) At what revenue level should you switch to self-hosted models?

agents.name: Agentic GitHub Bounties
agents.prompt: Research automated GitHub bounty/issue completion as revenue. (1) Platforms: Gitcoin, Bountysource, IssueHunt, Algora, Open Collective bounties. (2) Average bounty value. (3) Can a DeepSeek CLI agent solve GitHub issues and submit PRs automatically? (4) Design pipeline: monitor bounty platforms → find solvable issues → clone repo → analyze code → generate fix → run tests → submit PR → claim bounty. (5) Success rate — what % of bounties can AI solve? (6) Types of issues AI can solve: documentation, tests, simple bug fixes, dependency updates, type annotations. (7) Revenue potential: bounties/month × avg value × success rate. (8) Legal — is AI PR submission allowed? (9) Real examples of AI solving GitHub issues.

agents.name: Productized Services via CLI Agents
agents.prompt: Design 'productized services' that are actually CLI agents running DeepSeek. A productized service looks like a human service but is fully automated. (1) Code audit service: customer submits repo URL → CLI agent analyzes → returns report. Price: $49-199/audit. (2) SEO audit service: submit URL → full analysis. Price: $29-99. (3) Resume review service: submit resume → AI feedback. Price: $19-49. (4) API documentation service: submit API spec → generate docs. Price: $99-299. (5) Database optimization service: submit schema → get recommendations. Price: $49-149. For each: build time, DeepSeek cost, margin, how to sell (own site vs marketplace like ProductHunt, AppSumo, MicroAcquire). (6) Can you sell on Gumroad or LemonSqueezy?

agents.name: Webhook-as-a-Service Agents
agents.prompt: Design agentic services that respond to webhooks and generate revenue. Architecture: (1) User registers webhook URL at your endpoint, (2) When event fires (GitHub push, Stripe payment, form submission), your agent processes it with DeepSeek, (3) Agent sends results back via webhook response or email. Products: (1) PR Review webhook — GitHub sends PR → agent reviews → posts comments. Price: $9/mo per repo. (2) Lead enrichment webhook — form submission → agent researches company → sends enriched data. Price: $0.10/lead. (3) Support ticket classifier — email webhook → agent categorizes → routes. Price: $0.05/ticket. (4) Invoice processor — receive invoice PDF → extract data → send to accounting API. Price: $0.25/invoice. All managed via CLI. (5) Revenue at 100 customers.

agents.name: Cron Job Revenue Agents
agents.prompt: Design CLI agents that run on cron schedules and generate passive revenue. (1) Daily market report agent — generates crypto/stock analysis, emails to paid subscribers. (2) Weekly competitor monitor — tracks competitor changes, alerts subscribers. (3) Daily job listing aggregator — collects and curates, emails premium list. (4) Hourly price tracker — monitors product prices, sends alerts. (5) Daily security scan — checks client websites for vulnerabilities. For each: cron schedule, DeepSeek calls per run, cost per run, pricing to customers, delivery method (email/webhook/Telegram), revenue at 50/100/500 subscribers. Architecture: all run on one VPS via cron, managed by CLI, zero human intervention.

agents.name: Agent Marketplace Comparison Matrix
agents.prompt: Create a definitive comparison matrix of ALL marketplaces where you can list AI agents/tools for organic distribution. Columns: (1) Marketplace name, (2) Monthly active users/buyers, (3) Listing fee, (4) Revenue share %, (5) Can list CLI tool?, (6) Can list API?, (7) Can list MCP server?, (8) Automated listing via API?, (9) Discovery mechanism, (10) Competition level (low/mid/high), (11) Average revenue per listing, (12) Time to first sale. Include: npm, PyPI, GitHub Marketplace, VS Code, Smithery.ai, RapidAPI, Zapier, Chrome Web Store, Raycast, Docker Hub, AWS Marketplace, Shopify App Store, Replit, Homebrew. Rank by: (distribution × low competition × ease of listing). Top 3 for a solo dev with CLI agents?

agents.name: License Key Infrastructure for CLI
agents.prompt: Design the complete license key infrastructure for monetizing CLI agents. Requirements: (1) User gets free tier by default, (2) Pays via Stripe/LemonSqueezy, (3) Receives license key, (4) Enters key in CLI (stored in ~/.config/agent/license), (5) CLI validates key on each run, (6) Usage is metered and capped per tier. Implementation options: (1) Keygen.sh — features, pricing, API. (2) LemonSqueezy license keys. (3) Gumroad license keys. (4) Self-hosted via Supabase. (5) Stripe + custom validation. For each: cost, features, API quality, CLI integration effort. (6) Offline validation — can you validate without phoning home? (7) Anti-piracy — how hard is it to crack a CLI license? Does it matter? (8) Simplest possible implementation.

agents.name: Agentic Arbitrage: Cheap AI → Expensive Output
agents.prompt: Identify all opportunities where DeepSeek costs $0.001 to process something but the output is worth $1-100+ to the buyer. This is the core arbitrage. (1) Code review: DeepSeek cost $0.002/review, human cost $50-200/review, sell for $5-20. (2) Legal document review: cost $0.005, human lawyer $200+, sell for $20-50. (3) Resume optimization: cost $0.003, career coach $100+, sell for $10-30. (4) Patent search: cost $0.01, patent attorney $500+, sell for $50-100. (5) Tax question answering: cost $0.005, CPA $200+, sell for $10-25. List 20 such arbitrage opportunities. For each: DeepSeek cost, human equivalent cost, viable selling price, margin %, distribution channel, legal risk. Rank by (margin × market size × ease of automation).

agents.name: 24/7 Agentic Operations via CLI
agents.prompt: Design the complete 24/7 autonomous operations stack for running multiple CLI agents that generate revenue. Everything managed from terminal. (1) Process management: PM2 vs systemd vs supervisord. (2) Monitoring: what to watch, how to alert (to your phone/Telegram). (3) Logging: structured logs, rotation, search. (4) Deployment: git push → auto-deploy. (5) Scaling: when to add capacity. (6) Backup: database, config, keys. (7) Security: API key rotation, rate limiting, DDoS protection. (8) Cost tracking: daily cost report via CLI. (9) Revenue tracking: daily revenue from Stripe via CLI. (10) Health checks: automated + self-healing. Provide the ACTUAL commands and tools. This should be a copy-paste operations manual for running an agent empire from terminal.

agents.name: Day 1 Action Plan: CLI Agent Revenue
agents.prompt: Create the IMMEDIATE action plan to start earning money with CLI agents TODAY. Not in 48 hours, not next week — today. What's the fastest path from zero to first dollar? (1) Identify the single CLI agent that can be built in <4 hours AND listed on a marketplace with existing buyers. (2) Step-by-step: minute 0-30 (scaffold), minute 30-60 (core logic + DeepSeek), minute 60-120 (packaging + testing), minute 120-180 (marketplace listing), minute 180-240 (live + monitoring). (3) Expected first sale timeline. (4) Which marketplace has fastest time-to-first-sale? (5) What's the minimum viable CLI agent that someone would pay $1 for? (6) Revenue day 1, week 1, month 1. Be ruthlessly practical. No theory, only action.
